name: Spinner
summary: Says that something is loading when its length is unknown, as a turning ring with a label.
description: A spinner is the indeterminate loading indicator: a ring turns while a request, a page or a part of it loads, and a label names what loads, shown or kept for assistive technology. Use it for short waits in a small area (a button, a panel); for a long or measurable wait, a Progress bar; for content whose layout is known, Skeletons. Other systems call it an activity indicator, a loading indicator or a progress circle.

anatomy.description: Root: a status live region holding the ring and the label. Carries the size.
The turning ring: a neutral circle with a brand arc. Hidden from assistive technology; the label carries the meaning.
Text naming what loads (Loading projects). Shown next to the ring, or visually hidden but still announced.

properties.name: Size
properties.description: Diameter and stroke of the ring.

options.description: Inline, in a button or a table cell (16 px).
Centered in an empty panel or page (32 px).

properties.name: Label
properties.description: What loads, as a short phrase (Loading projects). Announced when the spinner appears.

properties.name: Show label
properties.description: Shows the label next to the ring. Hidden, it stays available to assistive technology.

states.description: The only state: the ring turns while the spinner is shown.

notes: The ring sits before the label, both centered on one row, separated by container.gap.
A spinner sits inline with what it replaces, or centered in the empty area it waits for.

name.text: A spinner is a status message, not a named control: its label is the text of the live region, announced when the spinner appears, whether the label is shown or visually hidden. The ring is hidden.

guidelines.text: A spinner reports a waiting state without taking focus: a polite status message that assistive technology announces when it appears, and whose text names what loads.

Render a div with role="status" (a polite, atomic live region) holding the label; insert it when the wait starts and remove or replace it when the content arrives. Keep the label visually hidden rather than absent: the ring alone says nothing to assistive technology.

The ring is a graphical object conveying the waiting state: its arc contrasts at least 3:1 with the surface in every color mode (5.79:1 light, 12.80:1 dark on the default surface) and with the still part of the ring (4.85:1 and 10.73:1).
The waiting state is conveyed by the movement and by the label, never by color alone. A shown label contrasts 12.87:1 (light) and 8.80:1 (dark) with the default surface.

A spinner turns for as long as the wait lasts. Shown alone while nothing else is usable, it is the preloader case that WCAG 2.2.2 describes; next to usable content, keep it short and prefer a determinate indicator when the length is known. Under reduced motion the ring stops turning and pulses its opacity instead.

An indeterminate progress indicator, also called an activity indicator, uses an animated image to indicate progress; people generally prefer a determinate indicator; keep indicators moving so people know something continues to happen, and remove them when the operation completes. Reduce automatic animations when Reduce Motion is on.
Mark the waiting message with the live region semantics so accessibility services announce it; describe the indicator's purpose.

guidelines: The label says what loads, in a short phrase: Loading projects, Saving, Signing in. Sentence case, no trailing punctuation.
Prefer a specific label to a generic Loading when the area has a name.

decisions.text: The still part of the ring is the third neutral base fill and the arc the accent brand fill (the Progress bar's track and indicator); a shown label is secondary text.
Three sizes from the size scale: small (16 px, 1.2 px stroke), medium (24 px, 2.4 px, the default) and large (32 px, 2.4 px).

A spinner is a polite status message whose text is its label, always present and visually hidden by default; the ring is hidden. One full turn takes four times the normal duration (1 s); under reduced motion the ring pulses between full and 40 % opacity instead of turning.

changelog.note: Initial draft (decisions ring-colors, sizes, status-message). A status live region with a turning ring and a visible or visually hidden label; sizes small, medium, large; no interaction state. Contrast, light / dark: arc on the default surface 5.79 / 12.80, arc on the ring 4.85 / 10.73, label 12.87 / 8.80.
